**Note to Users**: This script is provided for methodological transparency. It demonstrates our exact workflow for processing raw site files into clean inputs. Use this document as a blueprint to format your own data to match the structures defined in the Data Dictionaries below.

```{r setup-file, include=FALSE}
rm(list = ls())
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman"); library(pacman)
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, readxl, here)

new.dirs <- list("data", "data/raw", "data/processed", "data/processed/supplementary", "figures", "figures/validation")
lapply(new.dirs, function (x) if (!dir.exists(x)) {dir.create(x, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)})

FILE_CLIMATE      <- "data/raw/Model in Excel/2 WB_Anantapur_Crop_Level.xlsx"
FILE_KC_RAW       <- "data/raw/Model in Excel/1 Kc Anantapur.xlsx"
FILE_FARM_DEMOS   <- "data/raw/Model in Excel/For Rutuja_Crop_System_Area_by_Production_System.xlsx"

# ==============================================================================
# MODEL CALIBRATION CONSTANTS
# Note: These values are not standard FAO-56 published parameters. They were 
# derived and calibrated to explicitly match the legacy Excel mathematical 
# behaviors for Grassland grazing regrowth and Napier grass decline.
# ==============================================================================
legacy_calibrations <- list(
  grazing_growth_rate   = 0.00458333333333333,
  grazing_drop_kc       = 0.20,
  grazing_max_kc        = 0.75,
  napier_decline_rate_1 = 0.000307692307692308,
  napier_decline_rate_2 = 0.000153846153846154
)

source("code/02_function_get_kc.R")

theme_baseR <- theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black"), strip.background = element_blank())
```

# Climatic Data (Forcing Variables)

The foundation of the water balance model requires continuous, daily forcing variables. Here, we extract daily Precipitation (P) and Reference Evapotranspiration (ET0) from our raw climate sheets. We also generate a monthly climatology summary to use for later visualizations.

### 📖 Data Dictionary: Climate Inputs

| Variable | Expected Constraints |
| --- | --- |
| **Date** | Continuous sequential dates (YYYY-MM-DD) |
| **Rainfall (mm)** | Numeric ($\geq 0$) |
| **ET0** | Numeric ($\geq 0$) |

```{r clim}
clim <- readxl::read_xlsx(FILE_CLIMATE, sheet = "Climate")

# Extract Precipitation
precip <- clim %>% 
  select(date = Date, p = `Rainfall (mm)`) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date), p = as.numeric(p))

# Defensive Data Validation
stopifnot(
  "Error: Precipitation contains missing values (NA)." = !any(is.na(precip$p)),
  "Error: Precipitation cannot be negative." = all(precip$p >= 0, na.rm = TRUE)
)

write.csv(precip, file = "data/processed/01_precipitation.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Extract ET0
et0.daily <- clim %>% 
  select(date = Date, et0 = ET0) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date), et0 = as.numeric(et0))

stopifnot("Error: ET0 contains missing values (NA)." = !any(is.na(et0.daily$et0)))
write.csv(et0.daily, file = "data/processed/02_et0.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Create Climatology Summary
climate_summary <- clim %>% 
  select(date = Date, p = `Rainfall (mm)`, temp = `Moy Temp`, et0 = ET0) %>%
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(date), p = as.numeric(p), 
    temp = as.numeric(temp), et0 = as.numeric(et0), 
    Year = format(date, "%Y"), Month = format(date, "%m")
  ) %>%
  group_by(Year, Month) %>%
  summarise(Temperature = mean(temp, na.rm = TRUE), Rainfall = sum(p, na.rm = TRUE), ET0 = sum(et0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Month) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), .fns = list(avg = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE), q05 = ~ quantile(.x, probs = 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), q95 = ~ quantile(.x, probs = 0.95, na.rm = TRUE)), .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"))

write.csv(climate_summary, file = "data/processed/03_climatology_for_figure.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# Soil Parameters

The hydrological model requires specific soil properties to determine infiltration and drainage dynamics. We extract the local soil type, its Water Holding Capacity (WHC), and Readily Available Water (RAW) constraints.

### 📖 Data Dictionary: Soil Properties

| Variable | Expected Constraints |
| --- | --- |
| **whc.mmpercm** | Numeric (Water Holding Capacity) |
| **raw** | Numeric (Readily Available Water limit) |

```{r soil-param}
soil.param <- readxl::read_xlsx(FILE_CLIMATE, sheet = "crop Kc _ param SOILS", range = "A2:D4")
colnames(soil.param) <- c("soil", "soil.type", "whc.mmpercm", "raw")

# Defensive Data Validation
stopifnot(
  "Error: Soil WHC must be numeric." = is.numeric(soil.param$whc.mmpercm),
  "Error: Soil RAW must be numeric." = is.numeric(soil.param$raw)
)

write.csv(soil.param, file = "data/processed/04_soil.parameters.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# Crop Parameters & Coefficients (Kc)

To model water demand, we need the physical constraints of the crops (rooting depth, irrigation) and their daily Crop Coefficient (Kc​) curves.

## Rooting Depth and Irrigation Constraints

### 📖 Data Dictionary: Crop Parameters

| Variable | Expected Constraints |
| --- | --- |
| **irrigation** | Categorical constraint: strictly `"irrigated"` or `"rainfed"` |
| **rooting_depth_cm** | Numeric constraint representing absolute depth |

```{r crop-param}
crop.param <- readxl::read_xlsx(FILE_CLIMATE, sheet = "CROP parameters")

crop.param <- crop.param[, !as.logical(sapply(crop.param, function(x) all(is.na(x))))]
crop.param <- crop.param %>% 
  filter(!if_all(everything(), is.na)) %>% filter(!if_all(2:4, is.na)) %>% select(-Ref)

colnames(crop.param) <- c("crop", "irrigation", "rooting_depth_cm")
crop.param <- crop.param %>%
  mutate(crop = str_to_title(gsub("_", " ", crop, perl = TRUE))) %>%
  mutate(irrigation = case_match(as.character(irrigation), "1" ~ "irrigated", "2" ~ "rainfed", .default = NA)) %>%
  mutate(crop.ID = match(crop, unique(crop))) %>%
  select(crop.ID, everything())

# Defensive Data Validation
stopifnot(
  "Error: Rooting depth must be numeric." = is.numeric(crop.param$rooting_depth_cm),
  "Error: Irrigation strings mismatch." = all(crop.param$irrigation %in% c("irrigated", "rainfed", NA))
)

write.csv(crop.param, file = "data/processed/05_crop.parameters.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## Crop Coefficient (Kc) Generation

Evapotranspiration is scaled based on the crop's growth stage. Here we use a hybrid approach: we dynamically generate mathematically defined Kc curves in R (FAO Segmented and Polynomials).

### Generate FAO Segmented Curves (R Native)

```{r generate-fao-kc}
# Wrap the read_xlsx call to silently suppress formatting warnings
kc.raw <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
  readxl::read_xlsx(FILE_KC_RAW, sheet = "Crop cycles Kc", range = "A2:AK16")
))

# Clean empty columns and rows
kc.raw <- kc.raw[, !as.logical(sapply(kc.raw, function(x) all(is.na(x))))]
kc.raw <- kc.raw[!kc.raw[[1]] %in% c(NA, "Sowing_date"), ]
kc.raw[[1]][1] <- "Sowing"
kc.raw[[1]][nrow(kc.raw)] <- "Harvest"

colnames(kc.raw)[1] <- "var"; colnames(kc.raw)[2] <- "FORMULE"
kc.raw$FORMULE <- as.numeric(as.character(kc.raw$FORMULE))
kc.raw[-1] <- lapply(kc.raw[-1], function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x)))

# Dynamically locate fruit trees
pome_idx <- which(colnames(kc.raw) == "Pomegranate")
names(kc.raw)[pome_idx - 1] <- "Month"
kc.raw.fruit <- kc.raw[, c("Month", "Pomegranate", "Sweet lime")]

# Use literal dot escaping (\\.) to clean readxl suffixes safely
colnames(kc.raw) <- gsub("\\.\\.\\.[0-9]+$", "", colnames(kc.raw))

# Safely drop columns
kc.raw <- kc.raw %>% 
  dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of(c("Month", "Pomegranate", "Sweet lime", "Groundnut_monsoon", "Groundnut_summer")))

write.csv(kc.raw, file = "data/processed/supplementary/01_crop_kc_curve_parameters_table.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(kc.raw.fruit, file = "data/processed/supplementary/02_fruit_kc_curve_parameters_table.csv", row.names = FALSE)

kc.raw.long <- kc.raw %>% pivot_longer(cols = -1, names_to = "crop") %>% mutate(crop = str_to_title(gsub("_|\\.", " ", crop, perl = TRUE)))

kc <- kc.raw.long %>% subset(stringr::str_detect(var, stringr::regex("kc", ignore_case = TRUE))) %>% rename(Kc = value, kc_var = var) %>%
  mutate(Kc_var = case_when(grepl("ini", kc_var, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Kc_ini", grepl("mid", kc_var, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Kc_mid", grepl("end", kc_var, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Kc_end", TRUE ~ kc_var))

doy <- kc.raw.long %>% subset(var %in% c("Sowing", "End of ini", "End of Dev", "End of Mid", "Harvest")) %>% rename(doy = value, doy_var = var) %>% mutate(doy = if_else(doy == 365.00, 366.00, doy))

kc.doy.key <- data.frame(doy_var = c("Sowing", "End of ini", "End of Dev", "End of Mid", "Harvest"), kc_var = c("Kc_ini", "Kc_ini", "Kc_mid", "Kc_mid", "Kc_end"))

doy <- left_join(doy, kc.doy.key, by = c("doy_var"))
kc.doy <- left_join(doy, kc, by = c("kc_var", "crop")) %>% arrange(crop, doy, Kc) %>% mutate(doy = as.numeric(doy), Kc = as.numeric(Kc))

kc.doy.crops <- kc.doy %>% select(crop, doy_var, doy, Kc) %>%
  mutate(doy_var = factor(doy_var, levels = c("Sowing", "End of ini", "End of Dev", "End of Mid", "Harvest"))) %>%
  arrange(crop, doy, doy_var)

# Build FAO Curves using the external engine function
kc_wide_build <- kc.doy.crops %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = doy_var, values_from = c(doy, Kc)) %>%
  rename(
    Sow = doy_Sowing, E_ini = `doy_End of ini`, E_dev = `doy_End of Dev`,
    E_mid = `doy_End of Mid`, Harv = doy_Harvest,
    K_ini = Kc_Sowing, K_mid = `Kc_End of Dev`, K_end = Kc_Harvest
  )

kc_segmented_ls <- lapply(1:nrow(kc_wide_build), function(i) build_fao_curve(kc_wide_build[i, ]))
kc_segmented <- bind_rows(kc_segmented_ls) %>%
  mutate(crop = str_to_title(gsub("_", " ", crop, perl = TRUE)))
```

### Generate Polynomial Curves (Groundnuts)

```{r generate-poly-kc}
### Generate Polynomial Curves (Groundnuts)

# Groundnut Summer (Sown on Jan 10th: DOY 10)
gs <- data.frame(doy = 1:366) %>%
  mutate(crop = "Groundnut Summer", 
         d = doy - 10, 
         kc = if_else(d >= 0 & d <= 104,
                      1.25*10^(-7)*d^4 - 2.82*10^(-5)*d^3 + 1.8*10^(-3)*d^2 - 2.49*10^(-2)*d + 0.3792, 0))

# Groundnut Monsoon (Sown on July 1st: DOY 183)
gm <- data.frame(doy = 1:366) %>%
  mutate(crop = "Groundnut Monsoon",
         d = doy - 182,  
         kc = if_else(d >= 0 & d <= 104, 
                      1.32*10^(-7)*d^4 - 2.99*10^(-5)*d^3 + 1.96*10^(-3)*d^2 - 3.02*10^(-2)*d + 0.4, 0))

kc_polynomial <- bind_rows(gm, gs) %>% select(-d)
```

### Generate Fruit Tree Curves (Monthly to Daily)

```{r generate-fruit-kc}
### Generate Fruit Tree Curves (Monthly to Daily)

raw_params <- read.csv("data/processed/supplementary/02_fruit_kc_curve_parameters_table.csv", check.names = FALSE)

# FIX: Standardize parameter column headers to Title Case to prevent case-mismatches down the pipeline
colnames(raw_params) <- stringr::str_to_title(gsub("_|\\.", " ", colnames(raw_params)))


kc_fruits <- bind_rows(
  generate_fruit_step("Pomegranate", raw_params),
  generate_fruit_step("Sweet Lime", raw_params)) # "Sweet lime" -> "Sweet Lime" to align with title case
```

### Generate Complex Schedules Natively & Merge

```{r kc-complex}
# Re-introduce No Crop with a strict 0 baseline
no_crop <- tibble(doy = 1:366, crop = "No Crop", kc = 0)
grassland_base <- kc_segmented %>% filter(crop == "Grasslands") %>% pull(kc)

# Pull calibrated logic from the configuration block
growth_rate  <- legacy_calibrations$grazing_growth_rate
napier_dec_1 <- legacy_calibrations$napier_decline_rate_1
napier_dec_2 <- legacy_calibrations$napier_decline_rate_2
graze_drop   <- legacy_calibrations$grazing_drop_kc 
max_bound    <- legacy_calibrations$grazing_max_kc  

grassland_sow <- kc_wide_build$Sow[kc_wide_build$crop == "Grasslands"]

# Apply parameterized logic using the external engine function
# The 0.01 baseline is now natively handled by the function defaults
grazed_thrice <- generate_grazed_legacy("Grazed Thrice", c(182, 243, 304), grassland_base, growth_rate, graze_drop, max_bound, grassland_sow)
grazed_1_aug  <- generate_grazed_legacy("Grazed 1 Aug", 213, grassland_base, growth_rate, graze_drop, max_bound, grassland_sow)
grazed_1_sept <- generate_grazed_legacy("Grazed 1 Sept", 244, grassland_base, growth_rate, graze_drop, max_bound, grassland_sow)
grazed_1_oct  <- generate_grazed_legacy("Grazed 1 Oct", 274, grassland_base, growth_rate, graze_drop, max_bound, grassland_sow)
grazed_1_nov  <- generate_grazed_legacy("Grazed 1 Nov", 306, grassland_base, growth_rate, graze_drop, max_bound, grassland_sow)

# Napier functions automatically apply the 0.01 baseline before their respective start dates
napier       <- generate_napier("Napier", 1, napier_dec_1, napier_dec_2)
napier_short <- generate_napier("Napier Short", 211, napier_dec_1, napier_dec_2)

kc.doy.crop.all <- bind_rows(
  kc_segmented, kc_polynomial, kc_fruits, no_crop,
  grazed_thrice, grazed_1_aug, grazed_1_sept, grazed_1_oct, grazed_1_nov, 
  napier, napier_short
) %>% arrange(crop, doy)

write.csv(kc.doy.crop.all, file = "data/processed/supplementary/04_crop_kc_by_doy_all_crops.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

### Validation: R-Generated vs. Excel Legacy

Let's visually verify that our dynamic R calculations perfectly match the legacy Excel formulas for overlapping crops.

```{r validate-kc, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, out.width="100%"}
### Validation: R-Generated vs. Excel Legacy

kc.wide <- readxl::read_xlsx("data/raw/Model in Excel/2 WB_Anantapur_Crop_Level.xlsx", 
                             sheet = "crop Kc _ param SOILS", 
                             range = "B19:AL387")
kc.wide <- as.data.frame(kc.wide[-c(1:2), ]) %>%
  select(where(~ !all(is.na(.)))) %>%
  select(-starts_with("0.."))

names(kc.wide)[1] <- "doy"

kc_excel_fallback <- kc.wide %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -doy, names_to = "crop", values_to = "kc") %>%
  mutate(
    crop = str_to_title(gsub("_", " ", crop, perl = TRUE)),
    doy = as.numeric(doy),
    kc = as.numeric(kc)
  )

# Identify crops that exist in BOTH our generated dataset and the legacy excel sheet
overlap_crops <- intersect(unique(kc.doy.crop.all$crop), unique(kc_excel_fallback$crop))

validation_df <- kc.doy.crop.all %>%
  filter(crop %in% overlap_crops) %>%
  mutate(Source = "Native R Code") %>%
  bind_rows(
    kc_excel_fallback %>%
      filter(crop %in% overlap_crops) %>%
      mutate(Source = "Legacy Excel")
  )

p_validate <- ggplot(validation_df, aes(x = doy, y = kc, color = Source, linetype = Source)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.7, linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ crop, scales = "fixed") +
  theme_baseR +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Legacy Excel" = "red", "Native R Code" = "blue")) +
  labs(title = "Validation: R-Generated vs. Legacy Excel Kc Curves", 
       subtitle = "Blue and Red lines should perfectly overlap, appearing purple.",
       x = "Day of Year", y = "Kc") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

print(p_validate)
ggsave(plot = p_validate, 
       filename = "figures/validation/R-Generated vs. Legacy Excel Kc Curves.pdf", width = 10, height = 5.625, units = "in")

# FIX: Use rounding tolerance to eliminate floating point noise (e.g., 6.8e-08 machine differences)
kc_mismatch_summary <- validation_df %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Source, values_from = kc) %>%
  mutate(abs_diff = round(abs(`Native R Code` - `Legacy Excel`), 5)) %>%
  group_by(crop) %>%
  summarise(
    max_mismatch  = max(abs_diff, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_mismatch = mean(abs_diff, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(max_mismatch > 0.01) %>%
  arrange(desc(max_mismatch))

cat("--- Crops with True Mismatching Kc Curves ---\n")
print(kc_mismatch_summary)

mismatching_crop_names <- kc_mismatch_summary %>% pull(crop)

kc_mismatch_crops <- validation_df %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Source, values_from = kc) %>%
  mutate(abs_diff = abs(`Native R Code` - `Legacy Excel`)) %>%
  subset(crop %in% mismatching_crop_names) %>% 
  arrange(desc(abs_diff))

write.csv(kc_mismatch_crops, file = "kc_mismatch_crops.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# Crop Systems by Rotations

A single field rarely grows just one crop. We must map complex multi-crop rotations (e.g., Groundnut/Tomato). This step links those rotations to their required soils and crop profiles.

```{r crop-systems}
crop.systems <- readxl::read_xlsx(FILE_CLIMATE, sheet = "All rotations")
crop.systems <- as.data.frame(t(crop.systems[c(1:4), -c(1, 2)]))
names(crop.systems) <- c("crop1_crop2_crop3", "crop.system", "n.rotation", "soil")

crop.systems <- crop.systems %>%
  mutate(WB = row.names(crop.systems)) %>%
  subset(!is.na(n.rotation)) %>%
  separate_wider_delim(WB, delim = " ", names = c(NA, "rotation"), too_many = "merge", cols_remove = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(crop.system = str_to_title(crop.system), rotation = str_to_title(gsub("_", " ", rotation, perl = TRUE))) %>%
  mutate(crop.system.ID = match(crop.system, unique(crop.system)), rotation.ID = match(rotation, unique(rotation))) %>%
  mutate(crop1_crop2_crop3 = str_to_title(gsub("_", " ", crop1_crop2_crop3, perl = TRUE))) %>%
  separate_wider_delim(crop1_crop2_crop3, "-", names = c("crop_1", "crop_2", "crop_3"), cols_remove = FALSE, too_few = "align_start") %>%
  select(crop.system.ID, crop.system, n.rotation, rotation, rotation.ID, soil, crop1_crop2_crop3, WB, everything()) %>% 
  relocate(crop1_crop2_crop3, .after = crop_3) %>% 
  relocate(WB, .after = last_col())
```

## Join Crop Rooting Depth & Irrigation Requirements

```{r join-crop-root-depth}
crop.systems.l <- crop.systems %>%
  select(-WB) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("crop_"), names_prefix = "crop_", names_to = "ncrop", values_to = "crop") %>%
  left_join(crop.param, by = "crop") %>%
  relocate(crop.ID, .after = crop) %>%
  mutate(crop.rotation.ID = paste0(crop, ".", rotation.ID))

write.csv(crop.systems.l, file = "data/processed/06_crop.systems.l.csv", row.names = FALSE)

cs.rot.irri <- crop.systems.l %>%
  mutate(Irrigation = if_else(irrigation == "irrigated", TRUE, FALSE)) %>%
  group_by(crop.system, rotation) %>%
  summarise(Irrigation = any(Irrigation), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Irrigation = if_else(Irrigation == TRUE, "Irrigated", "Rainfed"))

crop.systems <- crop.systems %>% left_join(cs.rot.irri, by = c("crop.system", "rotation")) %>% relocate(Irrigation, .after = crop.system)

write.csv(crop.systems, file = "data/processed/07_crop.systems.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## Map Final Kc Curves to Systems

We now map our newly merged kc.doy database to the physical rotation schedules.

```{r map-kc-curves}
crop.systems.l.kc <- crop.systems.l %>% 
  select(rotation.ID, rotation, crop.rotation.ID, crop.system.ID, crop.system, soil, ncrop, crop, crop.ID, irrigation, rooting_depth_cm) %>%
  left_join(kc.doy %>% arrange(doy, crop), by = "crop", relationship = "many-to-many")

crop.rotation.kc.ls <- split(crop.systems.l.kc, crop.systems.l.kc$rotation)
save(crop.rotation.kc.ls, file = "data/processed/08_crop.rotation.kc.ls.Rdata")

crop.systems.kc.ls <- split(crop.systems.l.kc, crop.systems.l.kc$crop.system)
save(crop.systems.kc.ls, file = "data/processed/supplementary/05_crop.systems.kc.ls.Rdata")
```

# Production System Composition: Crop Systems by Area

To evaluate water potential at the macro level, we scale field-level data up using landscape demographics (area in hectares of each crop system).

```{r ps-composition}
ps_area <- readxl::read_xlsx(FILE_FARM_DEMOS, sheet = "Farm Type structure")

ps_area <- ps_area %>%
  subset(!is.na(WB)) %>%
  full_join(crop.systems %>% select(crop.system, WB), by = "WB") %>% relocate(crop.system, .before = 1) %>%
  mutate(crop.system = case_match(WB, "WB Rice/Banana" ~ "Rice/Banana", "WB Grazed_Once" ~ "Grasslands (Grazed Once)", "WB Rice/Napier" ~ "Rice/Napier", .default = crop.system)) %>%
  subset(!is.na(`Cropping system`)) 

ps_by_cs_area <- ps_area %>%
  select(-`Cropping system`, -WB) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -crop.system, names_to = "production_system_period", values_to = "area_ha") %>%
  subset(!is.na(area_ha) & !area_ha == 0) %>%
  mutate(
    time_period = str_extract(production_system_period, "(?<=\\()\\d{4}s?(?=\\))"),
    production_system = str_remove(production_system_period, "\\s*\\(\\d{4}s?\\)$"),
    time_period = if_else(is.na(time_period), "2022", time_period)
  ) %>%
  select(production_system_period, time_period, production_system, crop.system, area_ha) %>%
  arrange(time_period, production_system) %>%
  group_by(production_system_period, time_period, production_system, crop.system) %>%
  summarise(area_ha = sum(area_ha), .groups = "drop")

write.csv(ps_by_cs_area, file = "data/processed/09_crop_system_area_by_production_system.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# Landscape Composition: Number of Farms

To evaluate water potential at the macro level, we scale field-level data up using landscape demographics (area in hectares of each crop system).

```{r farm-counts}
farms_count_df <- readxl::read_xlsx(FILE_FARM_DEMOS, sheet = "Archetype Village") %>%
  rename(production_system = `Production System`, time_period = Period, number_of_farms = Number_of_Farms)
```
